$comment: Neutral shipped <sys/mount.h> (Darwin/BSD), added by the SQLite-CLI-for-arm64-Darwin cycle. sqlite's os_unix.c calls statfs()/fstatfs() to decide whether a database lives on a local, writable filesystem, and reads exactly two members of the result — `f_flags` (against MNT_RDONLY / MNT_LOCAL) and `f_fstypename`. ★★ THE SIZE OF `struct statfs` IS SAFETY-CRITICAL, WHICH IS WHY EVERY FIELD CARRIES AN EXPLICIT `offset`. sqlite declares `struct statfs fsInfo;` as a CALLER STACK SLOT (sqlite3.c:46491) and the kernel writes ALL 2168 bytes of it. Under-declaring the record does not produce a diagnostic of any kind — it produces a stack smash. The explicit-offset channel (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-UNION-OVERLAY; the mechanism is ALL-OR-NONE per struct, enforced at shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp:2124-2133) is used here NOT because anything overlaps but because it makes every byte position a stated, reviewable fact instead of a value re-derived from field widths — the same reason the macho arm of sys/stat.json:120-146 moved onto it. THE COST, stated plainly and identically to that precedent: this struct no longer DERIVES its offsets, so a future width edit will not self-correct; the interner still computes size = alignUp(max field extent, align) = alignUp(2140+28, 8) = 2168, so a slip in the TAIL is caught by the total while a slip in the MIDDLE is caught only by the offsets being read. ★ LAYOUT MEASURED against MacOSX26.4.sdk (extracted read-only at /tmp/apple_sdk_probe/MacOSX26.4.sdk/usr/include; nothing from the SDK is copied into this repo) and then re-measured by compiling an LP64 replica and printing sizeof/offsetof for every row: sizeof 2168, _Alignof 8, f_fsid@48 f_owner@56 f_flags@64 f_fstypename@72 f_mntonname@88 f_mntfromname@1112 f_flags_ext@2136 f_reserved@2140. On LP64 arm64 Darwin `struct statfs` IS the __DARWIN_STRUCT_STATFS64 body — mount.h:105 defines the macro and mount.h:133 expands it as `struct statfs` under `#if __DARWIN_64_BIT_INO_T`, which is 1 there; the pre-64-bit-inode `struct statfs` at mount.h:139+ is the #else arm and is NOT what we build against. `struct statfs64` is deliberately NOT shipped: mount.h:125-129 gates it on `!__DARWIN_ONLY_64_BIT_INO_T`, and on arm64 that symbol is 1, so the tag does not exist on our target and inventing it would let code compile here that Apple's own headers reject. MFSTYPENAMELEN is 16 (mount.h:94) and MAXPATHLEN is 1024 (sys/param.h:196 → sys/syslimits.h:103) — the two array bounds that make the total 2168 rather than something else; both are stated as literals in the field types so this record does not silently change shape if another descriptor's constant moves. ★ `f_fsid` is a WHOLE `fsid_t`, not a pair of flat ints, because it is a composite in C and a caller may assign or pass it by value — the same reasoning that put `st_mtimespec` in sys/stat.json's macho arm rather than leaving only the flattened scalars. Its tag `fsid` is declared FIRST in the `structs` array below and referenced BY NAME from the `f_fsid` field (source order IS the dependency order; a struct publishes its tag to the descriptor's name vocabulary only after it is selected — shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp:2143-2156, D-CSUBSET-DARWIN-BSD-STRUCT-BY-NAME). Its 8-byte size and 48-byte offset are MEASURED; the `{ int32_t val[2] }` member shape and the `fsid` tag spelling are the Darwin convention and were NOT measurable in the SDK slice (sys/_types/_fsid_t.h is not in it) — labelled INFERRED, tracked at D-FFI-DARWIN-FSID-T-SHAPE. The bare `fsid_t` typedef is published alongside with a byte-identical inline body so it interns to the SAME TypeId as the tag (the windows.json record convention), which is what lets a caller write `fsid_t id = fsInfo.f_fsid;`. ★ MNT_RDONLY 0x00000001 (mount.h:194) and MNT_LOCAL 0x00001000 (mount.h:222) are the two flags sqlite tests; MFSNAMELEN 15 (mount.h:93) and MFSTYPENAMELEN 16 (mount.h:94) ship because they are the names a caller needs to size or bound `f_fstypename` and are measured in the same read. The rest of the MNT_* flag wall, the fhandle/getmntinfo/vfsconf surface, and `struct vfsstat` are NOT shipped — no consumer, and each unmeasured row in a file that SHADOWS the real header (include_path_resolve.hpp:60-75, Descriptor → Source → NotFound; this file therefore also takes over on a NATIVE macOS host, where the SDK header is used today via D-INCLUDE-ANGLE-SOURCE-FALLBACK) is a silent-wrong-answer risk rather than a fail-loud gap. Tracked at D-FFI-DARWIN-SYS-MOUNT-PARTIAL. ★ NO `symbols` AND NO `library` KEY: `statfs` (unistd.json:40) and `fstatfs` (unistd.json:41) are ALREADY shipped and ALREADY export-verified by a real dlopen+dlsym run on an actual Mac (.plans/_deferred-anchor-registry.md:740); both spell the out-parameter `ptr<void>`, so this record introduces NO duplicate type and nothing in unistd.json needs to change to 'match' it (#47 / shipped_type_consistency.cpp — MEASURED: `statfs` appears in shippedLibs today only as that one function symbol row, never as a struct or typedef). Declaring nothing here also means including this header eager-imports nothing (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT — an unexported name in `symbols` breaks EVERY binary's LOAD, macho exit 127). Gated availableObjectFormats:[macho] — an elf/pe #include fails loud (the windows.json:5 [pe] precedent, inverted); Linux's `struct statfs` is a completely different 120-byte record and must never silently borrow this layout.
